title: The read of the rwb-case reference-data contract that returns a table of values is not specified
source: Ownership Map v1 api rows GET /admin/lists/{listCode} and POST /admin/reference-loads (owner P3, ASM-A6-api-4); Template and Rules v1 R3 default ruling (parameters and reference data to P3); legacy RWB-E1-064 AC1 and section 3
section: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-07; Ownership Map api GET /admin/lists/{listCode}
description: The dictionary slice reads its lists of values (LOV-ROLE, the refresh-cycle list) through the rwb-case reference-data contract instead of a monolith endpoint, and it submits its governance load through the same contract. The Ownership Map gives the owner (P3) and two admin paths, but no source names an operation that returns a whole reference table by table code to a consuming service, nor its parameters, its answer shape or its cache rule. The load path POST /admin/reference-loads is named; the read path is not.
evidence: Ownership Map api['GET /admin/lists/{listCode}'].owner = P3, ruling: the list and reference-load paths move to rwb-case under the R3 default ruling; TSD v5 P4 appendix T-A API-P4-004 to API-P4-010. No source gives a consumer-facing table read.
proposed: Publish the read as GET /api/recovery/case/v1/reference-data/{tableCode} on the rwb-case base with its fake, one hop and a 2 s timeout, and read every list through it; never write a list as a constant in code.

title: The field-level detail of the five dictionary schemas and the login wording of the contract baseline are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-064 Data table and AC1 to AC8; TSD P1 v3 Appendix T-A; API Specification v4 admin dictionary and contract paths
section: Legacy RWB-E1-064 Data; TSD P1 v3 T-A
description: The legacy story names the five tables, the 122 objects, the 1,366 fields and the field attributes, and the API specification gives the property names of the resource, but no source fixes which property of each of the five schemas is required, which is nullable, the exact length of each string, or the wording of the per-service login behind the security scheme. The baseline has to fix them once so that the five operations and the reference-table handler can be faked.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-064 Data table lists the attributes without required flags; API Specification v4 gives the resource properties only; TSD P1 v3 T-A gives purpose, parameters and error codes.
proposed: Fix the property names from the API specification character for character, set the required flags and lengths at the baseline review, and name the login as the rwb_source_data login (DP-02).

title: No deployment value, probe timing, alert threshold or incident route exists for the dictionary slice
source: Legacy RWB-E1-064 (no deployment section); Architecture v5 slides 20 and 41; Non Functional Specification v3
section: Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12 and s16
description: The legacy story is an application story and carries no chart, no values file, no probe, no alert and no runbook. The target needs all of them for the five admin operations, the reference-table handler and the dictionary migration step, and no source gives a replica count, a resource size, a probe path, a timing, an alert threshold, a window or an incident route.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-064 has no section 12 deployment content; Architecture v5 slide 20 names the service template and shared libraries without values; no source carries a values file for rwb-source-data.
proposed: Carry every deployment value as a chart value named in the story, set per environment by the platform team, and never hard-code one.

title: The sandbox scope per service and the placement of the generator module are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 3, 4 and 12; Architecture v5 slides 11, 20 and 29
description: The legacy story describes one sandbox database built from the monolith schema. The target has 19 schemas and 19 services, and no source says whether the sandbox is one database per service release or one shared sandbox across the 19 services, nor whether the synthetic data generator ships inside the service artefact or as a separate build module of the repository.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-065 AC1 'the sandbox exists' names one database; Architecture v5 slide 29 forbids a cross-schema read; no source fixes the build placement of the generator.
proposed: One DEV sandbox database per service release, rwb_sandbox for rwb-source-data, with the generator as a separate build module that the service artefact does not contain.

title: The contract of a build tool is not described by any source document
source: Legacy RWB-E1-065 section 12 stage description; TSD P1 v3 T3.1; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12
description: No source of this run describes the interface of a build stage, so the sandbox contract is read as the pipeline stage interface with its input and output profile. The field-level definition of the seed profile (types, lengths, required flags and the exact wording of the pattern rule) is given by no source either, so the baseline fixes the five profile elements and leaves the field-level detail to the review.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-065 section 12 describes the stage in prose only; TSD P1 v3 T3.1 lists the sandbox objects without a profile schema.
proposed: Publish the stage interface and its input and output profile, with the four fixtures (full seed, empty seed, refused seed, timeout) and drift detection as a build failure.

title: The sandbox database scope and its read-only role name are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-065 AC2 and AC7; Ownership Map v1 (no sandbox row); Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29
description: The legacy story asserts that the sandbox is readable and extractable and that no clear personal value sits outside the ACE tables, but it names no database, no role and no grant. For the 19-service target no source fixes whether the sandbox is one database per service release and what the read-only role is called.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-065 AC2 'it is readable and extractable'; the Ownership Map carries no sandbox entry; Architecture v5 slide 11 gives one login per service and no sandbox login.
proposed: One DEV database rwb_sandbox per service release with the build database rwb_sandbox_next, and the read-only role rwb_sandbox_read granted SELECT only.

title: The append path, its authorisation handling and its 404 semantics are a target choice, not a legacy value
source: Legacy RWB-E1-066 AC5 to AC7; API Specification v4 POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions; Ownership Map api POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions (owner P1, ASM-A6-api-1)
description: The legacy writer was an in-process Java interface with no path and no status code, so no source fixes the append path, the status code for an idempotency conflict, the handling of the authorisation header, or whether an out-of-scope case answers 403 or 404. The scope check is now a cross-service call to rwb-case and not a local join, which the legacy ACs do not describe.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-066 describes InteractionLedgerWriter as an interface; API Specification v4 declares the path with x-module P3 while the Ownership Map gives the ledger to P1.
proposed: Append as POST /interactions on the rwb-source-data base, 403 without Case record C, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope case with MSG-P4-003, 409 for a reused Idempotency-Key with a different body, and publish all of it in RWB-P1-E1066-CON.

title: The exact ledger resource path, the login wording and the field-level required flags are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-066 section 12; API Specification v4 Interaction schema; TSD P3 v3 T-A (API-P3-014, API-P3-015); Ownership Map api POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions
section: Legacy RWB-E1-066 section 12; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-18
description: The API specification declares the interaction paths with x-module P3 and names the Interaction resource, and the Ownership Map rules the ledger to P1, but no source gives the P1 resource path, the split of the error statuses, which ledger values are required for a Workbench event, which are nullable, or the exact length of each property.
evidence: API Specification v4 POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions x-module P3; Ownership Map ruling: the owner is P1 and rwb-case reads the ledger through the P1 contract; TSD P3 v3 T-A gives purpose and error codes only.
proposed: Fix the path as /interactions on the service base, name the login as the rwb_source_data login, take the property names from the API specification and settle the required flags at the baseline review.

title: No deployment value, alert threshold, probe timing or incident route exists for the ledger writer
source: Legacy RWB-E1-066 (no deployment section); Architecture v5 slide 20; Non Functional Specification v3
section: Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12 and s16
description: The legacy story assumed the table, the writer and the incident hook sat in one monolith release and carries no chart, values file, probe, alert, threshold or route. The target needs all of them, including an alert on the append-only trigger, and no source gives any value.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-066 has no deployment content; the ledger incident LEDGER_WRITE_FAILED has no agreed alert text, threshold, window or route in the source set.
proposed: Carry every deployment value, threshold, window and route as a named chart value set per environment, and fail the release when the append-only trigger is missing.

title: The mapping of the document fact and the timer fact onto the target event types is not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-067 EV-16 DocumentStored and EV-19 TimerBreached; Architecture v5 slide 15 event catalogue rows 16 and 19; Ownership Map api (no rwb-source-data consumer row)
section: Legacy RWB-E1-067 AC2, AC4, AC6, AC7, AC8
description: The legacy intake names its own application events EV-16 DocumentStored and EV-19 TimerBreached. The target catalogue carries rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 and rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1 and does not list rwb-source-data as a consumer of either, so no source says that the two legacy facts map onto those two CloudEvents types or that the ledger intake subscribes to them.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-067 section 12 event list; Architecture v5 slide 15 rows 16 and 19 give the CloudEvents names and their producers; the consumer column names no rwb-source-data row.
proposed: Read the two facts as rows 16 and 19 of the Architecture v5 catalogue and fix both rows in the intake map of RWB-P1-E1067-CON, with the producer signing off its row.

title: The format and version label of the ledger intake map are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-067 section 12 event map; Architecture v5 slide 15; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12
description: The legacy story carries the six consumed events as a table in prose. The target publishes the map as a versioned contract artefact, and no source fixes its schema, its version label, where it is published, or the exact target event names that carry the document fact and the timer fact.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-067 section 12 lists the events without a file or a label; no source describes a map document for the intake.
proposed: Publish contract/ledger-intake-map-v1.yaml with one row per consumed event type, its version label as a field of the document, and the six rows of section 12.4 of the contract.

title: The guarantee claim read of rwb-guarantee and the case-existence answer are not in the Work Package's contract list
source: Legacy RWB-E2-010 AC2 and AC4; Work Package B-P1-02 contract dependencies RWB-P3-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E2004-CON; Architecture v5 slide 18
section: Legacy RWB-E2-010 AC2, AC4; Template and Rules v1 R5.4
description: The stage 2 build reads treatment facts through the treatment contract and guarantee claim facts through the guarantee contract of rwb-guarantee, and checks that a case exists through rwb-case. The Work Package lists only two C dependencies and neither is the guarantee contract nor the case-existence answer, so the name and the shape of the guarantee claim read are fixed by no source and S3 is not built until wave 3.
evidence: Work Package B-P1-02 RWB-P1-E2010-APP contract dependencies: RWB-P3-E1043-CON, RWB-P3-E2004-CON. Architecture v5 slide 18 gives rwb-guarantee the TCG and insurance claims without a contract.
proposed: Add the guarantee claim read as a C dependency with its fake, returning no claim until S3 is built, and take the case-existence answer from the rwb-case case contract, faked the same way.

title: The workflow and activity names of the stage 2 build are a target design choice
source: Legacy RWB-E2-010 section 4 (stage 2 step of JOB-02); Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-02; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-10
description: The legacy stage 2 step is a step of the monolith daily case run and carries no workflow name. The target runs it as a Temporal workflow on the rwb-source-data task queue, and no source names the workflow, its activities, their retry policy or the rerun rule for a business date.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-010 section 4 describes the step in prose; Architecture v5 slide 44 gives JOB-02 to rwb-source-data without naming a workflow.
proposed: Stage2ProductWorkflow on queue rwb-source-data in namespace rwb-recovery with the activities snapshot(page), writeDp04Page, checkActiveCount and stampDp04, started by rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1.

title: The expected-by time of DP04 is assumed from the decision log and stated by no source
source: Legacy RWB-E2-010 AC1 and section 3 (DL11 reference); TSD P1 v3 T3.1 data_product; Architecture v5 slide 41 P1 freshness
description: The stage 2 build waits for the treatment product to be fresh before it snapshots it, and the legacy story took the expected-by time of DP04 from decision log row DL11. No source document of this run states the expected-by time of DP04, so the freshness gate of the build cannot be fixed from the source set.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-010 section 3 cites DL11 for the DP04 expected-by time; the data_product row in TSD P1 v3 T3.1 gives the product without a time.
proposed: Carry 08:00 as the DP04 expected-by time, as DL11 assumed, until the data steward records the value in the data_product row.

title: The field-level DP04 record schema and the shape of the guarantee claim read are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E2-010 Data table; API Specification v4 GET /data-products/{productCode}/records; Architecture v5 slide 18 S3
section: Legacy RWB-E2-010 Data; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12
description: The contract has to publish the DP04 record and the guarantee claim read it consumes, but no source fixes the required flags, the lengths and the formats per property of the snapshot and ACE rows, nor the answer shape of the guarantee claim read of rwb-guarantee.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-010 Data table lists the DP04 fields by name; API Specification v4 gives the record resource properties only; Architecture v5 slide 18 gives S3 the claims without a contract.
proposed: Fix the property names from the legacy data rows and API Specification v4, leave the required flags and lengths to the baseline review, and fake the guarantee claim read.

title: No deployment value, threshold, probe timing or fixture owner exists for the stage 2 build
source: Legacy RWB-E2-010 (no deployment section); Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-02; Non Functional Specification v3
section: Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12 and s16
description: The stage 2 build is the stage 2 step of the daily JOB-02 run in the target and needs a chart, values, probes, lag and stale thresholds, alerts and a runbook, and its test data needs an owner. The legacy story carries none of them and no source gives a replica count, a resource size, a threshold, a timing or a fixture owner.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-010 has no deployment content; no source carries a values file or a test-data owner for the stage 2 build.
proposed: Carry every deployment value, threshold and timing as a named chart value set per environment, and name the fixture owner at the wave 2 entry check.
